common.patient_context: This suite is for advanced breast cancer. The executable protocol retains other NCCP tumour indications; breast trial results and breast counselling must be labelled as such.
common.treatment_goal: Aim to slow or shrink advanced breast cancer and help symptoms while balancing side effects. Duration depends on benefit, tolerability and the agreed plan; a fixed number of cycles or a guaranteed survival improvement is not promised.

mechanism.clinician: Vinca alkaloid; inhibits tubulin polymerisation, disrupting mitotic microtubules and cell division atG2–M.
mechanism.patient: Vinorelbine disrupts the tiny structures a cell needs to divide. This can stop cancer cells multiplying. Healthy blood-forming cells, gut cells and nerves can also be affected.

body_map.title: Blood counts and infection
body_map.text: White blood cells can fall, raising the risk of infection. Anaemia can cause tiredness or breathlessness; low platelets can cause bruising or bleeding. Blood tests guide delays and dose changes. Fever, shaking chills or feeling suddenly unwell need the oncology emergency contact immediately.

body_map.title: Constipation, nausea and mouth problems
body_map.text: The bowel can slow down and nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea or sore mouth can occur. Use the prescribed bowel and anti-sickness plan. Severe abdominal pain, swelling, repeated vomiting or inability to pass stool/gas needs urgent assessment for ileus; do not simply take extra laxatives.

body_map.title: Tingling, numbness or weakness
body_map.text: Nerve effects may change sensation, grip, walking or bowel movement. Report changes early because the next dose may need to wait or be reduced.

body_map.title: Fatigue, hair and liver tests
body_map.text: Tiredness, hair thinning/loss and liver-test changes can occur. Pace activities and tell the team if eating, drinking or daily tasks become difficult.

body_map.title: Uncommon serious symptoms
body_map.text: New chest pain, sudden or worsening breathlessness, or severe allergic symptoms need urgent medical help. Previous heart disease and interacting medicines need review before treatment.

consent_topics: Purpose and alternatives for the person’s advanced breast cancer, including other systemic treatment or supportive care according to goals.
Possible benefit is uncertain; response is reviewed and treatment can be paused, changed or stopped.
Low blood counts, infection/sepsis, fatigue, nausea/vomiting, bowel problems, neuropathy, hair change and uncommon serious lung/heart/allergic toxicity.
Fertility and pregnancy planning before treatment; discuss sperm/egg preservation where relevant. Do not breastfeed.
HPRA supplements: contraception during treatment and for 7 months afterwards for women,4 months for men; confirm the exact product and individual advice.
No independent clinical or oncology pharmacy sign-off is claimed by this software.
baseline: Confirm exact indication, ECOG 0–2, previous treatments and original/current dose.
FBC with differential, renal/liver function and neuropathy assessment.
Review infection in the preceding 2 weeks, allergies, pregnancy/breastfeeding, bowel problems, heart disease and all medicines/supplements/vaccines.
common.heart_monitoring: Review cardiovascular history and new symptoms. These monotherapy NCCP protocols do not mandate the serial LVEF/echo schedule used for anthracyclines or trastuzumab; arrange cardiac tests when clinically indicated.
supportive_plan_common: Individual antiemetic plan differs by route; list routine and rescue medicines separately.
Discuss constipation prevention, hydration/diet where appropriate and prescribed laxatives; regular opioid use increases the need for a bowel plan.

No routine steroid premedication, G-CSF, antibacterial, antiviral or PJP prophylaxis is mandated by these NCCP monotherapy documents. Consider additional prevention based on individual risk/local policy; do not create a generic automatic prescription.
Gastric protection is a consideration for high gastrointestinal-bleed risk, not a universal drug.

Confirm strong CYP3A4 inhibitors/inducers, P-gp modulators, phenytoin, itraconazole, warfarin and live vaccines. Yellow fever vaccine is contraindicated. Avoid grapefruit per NCCP; do not self-start supplements.
common.urgent_contact: Use the treating unit’s 24-hour emergency number and local fever threshold. Contact immediately for fever/chills, sudden illness, breathlessness/chest pain, uncontrolled vomiting, severe abdominal pain/obstruction symptoms, bleeding or severe allergy. Do not wait until the next visit.

00232.title: Intravenous vinorelbine for advanced breast cancer

schedule.dose: 30 mg/m² onDays 1 and 8 every 21 days. Consultant may consider 25 mg/m² for poor marrow reserve; the dose is individualised after toxicity.
schedule.planned_duration: Repeated 21-day cycles until progression/unacceptable toxicity; team review determines continuation.

timeline.event: Assessment, blood tests and medicine review; agree bowel/rescue antiemetic plan and IV access.
Blood-count review, IVvinorelbine, then saline flush; observe the IV site.
Repeat blood-count review before the second infusion; symptoms and previous dose effects may alter treatment.
No scheduled vinorelbine; recovery period with symptom monitoring. Infection can occur between visits.
Repeat cycle only after the team checks benefit, counts, liver/renal function and nerve/bowel symptoms.

00232.administration: NCCP specifies 50 mL sodium chloride 0.9% over 15 minutes followed by 250 mL saline. Current Navelbine SmPC says 6–10 minutes: product/local-pharmacy reconciliation is required. Do not promise a total visit length; preparation, tests and observation add time.
00232.route_safety: For IV use only; intrathecal administration may be fatal. Oral and IV vinorelbine are not interchangeablemg-for-mg. Stop infusion and tell staff immediately about pain, burning, swelling or leakage at the IV site; extravasation can damage tissue.

monitoring.NCCP: FBC, renal/liver function before each cycle; neuropathy each cycle.
monitoring.supplement: Navelbine SmPC requires blood counts on the day of each administration, includingDay 8. Do not omitDay 8 checks based on the NCCP cycle-only wording.
monitoring.nadir: Neutrophil nadir commonly 7–14 days; this is not a guarantee that other days are safe.
monitoring.source_conflicts: NCCP ANC exclusion<1.5 versus table 100%at≥1/75%at 0.5–0.99; platelet 75–99 table reduction versus current Navelbine<100 delay. Clinical/pharmacy reconciliation required; software must not clear these conflicts.

antiemetic.current_classification: Minimal IVrisk (<10% untreated vomiting risk category)
antiemetic.routine: No routine prophylaxis required by NCCP minimal-risk pathway.
antiemetic.rescue: Prescriber selects an as-needed medicine according to symptoms, constipation, QT/interactions and local policy. Reassess before future doses if nausea/vomiting occurs.

logistics: Two infusion visits per 21-day cycle, with blood tests before doses. Peripheral cannula or existing access according to the treating service; a port is not automatically required.
Wear clothing allowing IV-site observation; report discomfort immediately.
No home vinorelbine capsules are part of this regimen. Keep an up-to-date medication list and emergency contact.

00259.title: Oral vinorelbine for advanced breast cancer

schedule.dose: ONCE WEEKLY. First 3 administrations 60 mg/m², total maximum 120 mg. From administration 4,80 mg/m² (maximum 160 mg) only after the team reviews nadirs and toxicity.60 or 50 mg/m²/lower may be needed.
schedule.planned_duration: Continue weekly while helpful and tolerated; no fixed total number of weeks.

timeline.event: Blood tests, medicines/bowel assessment and a written weekly capsule/antiemetic plan. Verify refrigerated storage and capsule strengths.
Three once-weekly doses, each only after blood-count clearance. Do not take the capsules every day.
Review all first-three nadirs; a severe or repeated low count prevents escalation. Do not increase the number of capsules yourself.
Continue once weekly at the current authorised dose; blood counts before each dose and symptom checks.
At least three reviewed administrations at 60 before any re-escalation decision; nadir history and other toxicity still apply.

administration: Take with some food; swallow capsules whole with water. Do not chew, suck or dissolve.
The exact total dose may require more than one capsule; pharmacy provides the strengths and number. Verify the weekly date, dose and capsule count each time.
Do not take another dose if vomiting occurs within a few hours. Contact the team and record the dose taken.
Do not swallow damaged capsules. Return them to pharmacy; immediately wash any contact with contents using water or saline.
Missed/late dose: contact the team for the next date. Do not double or move the weekly schedule yourself. This is pragmatic medication-safety advice, not an extra NCCP catch-up schedule.
00259.route_safety: Oral 60/80 mg/m² and IV 25/30 mg/m² have pharmacokinetic equivalence references, but never convertmg-for-mg or swap routes yourself. Dose rules and schedules differ.

monitoring.blood_counts: NCCP: before each treatment. HPRA: on the day of every new administration. ANC<1.5 or platelets<100 requires delay until recovery.
monitoring.renal_liver: NCCP: renal/liver function at cycle start; the regimen is weekly. Use the actual prescribed testing plan, not an invented four-week interval. Liver abnormalities can require 60,50 or stopping; do not self-adjust.
monitoring.history: Track nadirs over first 3 doses, during 80 mg/m² treatment, and the 3 doses at 60 following reduction; current pre-dose blood counts are not a substitute.
monitoring.symptoms: Check constipation/obstruction, neuropathy, oral intake, infection and dose adherence each contact.

antiemetic.current_classification: Moderate–high oral category (≥30% untreated emesis category)
antiemetic.routine_options: NCCP Table 5: one 5-HT3 antagonist—ondansetron 8–16 mg totaldaily OR granisetron 1–2 mg totaldaily.
antiemetic.subsequent_days: Table 5 says continue daily; for once-weekly vinorelbine the prescriber must state the number of days. Do not automatically turn this into indefinite daily treatment or import an IV moderate steroid/NK 1 schedule.
antiemetic.rescue: A separate locally approved as-needed plan; check constipation and QT/interactions. Avoid duplicate 5-HT3 agents. Ondansetron can worsen constipation.
antiemetic.patient_instruction: Take the anti-sickness medicine exactly as prescribed before/around the weekly capsule dose; contact the team if it is not controlling symptoms.

capsules.table_note: NCCP p 2 contains eleven BSA bands for 60 and 80 mg/m², with caps 120/160 mg. The 50 mg/m² hepatic/toxicity target has no matching column; pharmacy calculation/rounding is needed.
capsules.storage: Current Vinorelbine Accord SmPC: refrigerator 2–8°C. Confirm the dispensed brand/pack instructions; keep in original packaging and out of children’s reach.
capsules.disposal: Return unused or damaged capsules to pharmacy; follow cytotoxic handling advice.

logistics: Home dosing still needs weekly blood tests and explicit team clearance. Arrange a reliable weekly routine and a way to contact the team before taking a dose if unwell.
Record actual dose, capsule strengths/count, date taken, vomiting and side effects in the passport. An unfilled date is not a request for patients to calculate treatment dates.
Ensure access to a refrigerator if required by the dispensed pack; discuss travel/transport with pharmacy.
